strengths: Well-motivated work addressing genuine bottlenecks in RLVR training (slow convergence, sparse rewards, hard prompts)
Mathematically grounded uncertainty-based rollout allocation using Student's t-confidence intervals
Comprehensive experimental validation across 7 diverse benchmarks with consistent improvements (1.4-2.5% on reasoning models, up to 20% on non-reasoning models)
Strong practical benefits: 2.4-2.7× faster training convergence and 13-14% shorter inference sequences
Novel application of ICL seeding within RLVR to break zero-reward symmetry, with demonstrated 4-10% recovery on hard prompts
Thorough ablation studies and sensitivity analysis demonstrating each component's contribution and robustness
Clear presentation with well-designed figures and comprehensive algorithm description
Demonstrated compatibility with recent state-of-the-art methods (GSPO)
weaknesses: Improvements over GSPO are incremental (1-2.5% on reasoning models where baselines are already competitive) rather than transformative
Limited theoretical novelty: each component (uncertainty sampling, ICL, entropy bonuses) relies on established techniques; their combination lacks deep integration insights
Experimental scope limited to Qwen models only; no evaluation on LLaMA, Mistral, or other mainstream LLM families
Design choices lack strong justification: why Student's t-distribution? Why the specific φ_q = λ√(log(1+T))/n_q formula? Why K=2 examples for ICL?
ICL seeding limitations underexplored: only 6-10% success rate on hard prompts; effectiveness on truly OOD problems unclear; requires embedding model dependency (Qwen3-Embedding-8B)
Technical details need clarification: Eq. 2 approximation assumes smooth behavior potentially problematic for small n_q; novelty measure relationship to entropy remains informal
Missing key comparisons with related methods (TreeRL, TreeRPO explicitly mentioned in related work)
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals for reported improvements
Computational cost analysis missing despite claims of 'lightweight implementation'; high GPU requirements (16×H200) limit reproducibility and accessibility
Limited ablation scope: hyperparameter sensitivity only varies λ_novelty and κ_clip, not n_base, T, or λ (exploration weight)
